summary: On node1, set up /srv/data as a btrfs subvolume (backed by a loop-mounted image at /var/lib/snapshots/srv-data.img, persisted via /etc/fstab) since no snapshot-capable filesystem or spare block device existed. Populated it with sample application data, took a read-only baseline snapshot (btrfs subvolume snapshot -r), then modified /srv/data (edited files, added an unauthorized file, deleted a log). Restored /srv/data to the exact baseline content by deleting the modified subvolume and recreating it from the read-only snapshot, verified via SHA-256 checksums that the restored content matches the baseline byte-for-byte and the tampered file is gone. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and data checksums pre-restart, issued a native reboot, polled until node1 exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and confirmed the btrfs mounts, subvolumes, and file checksums all recovered identically to the pre-restart/baseline state after boot.
actions_performed: Created a 2G sparse image, loop-attached it, formatted as btrfs
Mounted top-level subvol at /mnt/btrfsroot and created a 'data' subvolume mounted at /srv/data
Added persistent fstab entries (loop,subvol=...) for both mountpoints
Populated /srv/data with sample application data and captured baseline SHA-256 checksums
Took a read-only btrfs snapshot 'snap-baseline' of the data subvolume
Modified /srv/data (edited files, deleted app.log, added tampered.log) and confirmed checksums diverged from baseline
Restored /srv/data by unmounting, deleting the modified subvolume, re-snapshotting 'snap-baseline' into a new writable 'data' subvolume, and remounting; verified checksums matched baseline exactly
Captured pre-restart boot_id and data health, issued sudo -n reboot, polled until node1 was reachable again
Verified boot_id changed after restart and that mounts, subvolumes, and file checksums fully recovered to baseline

evidence.summary: Confirmed no LVM/btrfs/spare disk existed; installed btrfs-progs, created loop-backed btrfs image, created 'data' subvolume mounted at /srv/data, added persistent fstab entries.
Populated /srv/data with app.conf, accounts.csv, logs/app.log; recorded baseline SHA-256 checksums; took read-only btrfs snapshot 'snap-baseline'.
Edited app.conf and accounts.csv, deleted logs/app.log, added logs/tampered.log; diff confirmed checksums differ from baseline.

evidence.requirement: Exact restoration of earlier snapshot content
evidence.summary: Deleted modified 'data' subvolume, recreated it from 'snap-baseline', remounted at /srv/data; checksums diff against baseline showed zero difference; tampered.log absent, app.log restored.

evidence.requirement: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (45805187-c3ef-45cb-bc40-b6ac5e8dbe08), mount state, and SHA-256 checksums of /srv/data matching the restored baseline.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledged and executed one node at a time
evidence.summary: Issued 'sudo -n reboot' via backgrounded nohup so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection; confirmed only node1 (the sole managed node) was restarted.

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed, proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: Polled node1 through connection resets/timeouts during reboot; once reachable, boot_id read 6e850278-372e-46e8-ae57-e2a7d0ca25d3 with uptime 0 min, differing from the pre-restart boot_id.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of filesystem snapshot setup and data
evidence.summary: Confirmed fstab-driven loop/btrfs mounts for /mnt/btrfsroot and /srv/data auto-recovered, both subvolumes (data, snap-baseline) intact, and /srv/data file checksums matched the original baseline exactly post-reboot.
